name: Git credentials prompt + GitHub integration foundation
description:
Request (from user, chat): when a git remote operation (fetch/pull/push) fails because the remote needs credentials and the project settings hold no access token, the platform must ASK the user for username + password, use them for that single operation only, and never store them anywhere (no project settings, no global git config, no credential store, no logs, no task card / chat payload).

In parallel, prepare the GitHub integration so a project can be connected to repositories on GitHub.

Existing starting point (verified in the codebase):
- api/codx/junior/engine/git_engine.py: PAT support already exists — DEFAULT_TOKEN_USERNAME = "x-access-token", TOKEN_ARG_PREFIX = "http.extraheader=", TOKEN_VALUE_MASK = "********", AUTH_ERROR_PATTERNS + AUTH_ERROR_HINT, get_git_access_token(), _token_args(), _mask_token_args(), _run_git(apply_token=...), fetch_remote(), pull_remote(), push_remote() (~line 3642+).
- api/codx/junior/settings.py: git_access_token / get_git_access_token() :330, has_git_access_token() :383, masked_git_access_token() :392, GIT_ACCESS_TOKEN_MASK :45.
- api/codx/junior/api/git.py: POST /git/repo/fetch :1060, /pull :1073, /push :1086, _ensure_success :338, GET /git/repo/info :364, /remotes :493.
- client/src/api/modules/repo.js:727 push(), + fetch/pull helpers.
- Existing GitHub pieces: api/codx/junior/security/github_oauth.py (GitHubOAuth - login only), api/codx/junior/misc/github.py (issue search), security/user_management.py (GITHUB_ADMINS).

Acceptance criteria:
1. Remote ops accept OPTIONAL transient credentials (username/password or token) per request; they are injected as a one-shot `-c http.extraheader=Authorization: Basic ...` (or equivalent) and never written to disk, never persisted in settings, never returned in responses, masked in logs and git command echoes.
2. When no credential is configured and git fails with an auth error, the API returns a structured, machine-readable marker (e.g. `requires_credentials: true` + hint) instead of a bare 400, and the client shows a dialog asking for username/password.
3. Password field is never echoed back to the client; any CISO/redaction path treats it as a secret.
4. Transient credentials live in request scope only (memory, no TTL cache keyed by token, no `.codx` writes, no audit payload with the value).
5. GitHub integration foundation: documented design + minimal, feature-flagged scaffolding (settings block for GitHub connection, repo listing/attach API surface, clone/remote wiring) so a project can be connected to a GitHub repo later.
6. Backend tests cover: masking, no-persistence, requires_credentials payload, and transient credential injection.

Credentials policy: if the run itself needs git remote credentials, ASK the user — never invent, never store them.
